q: How do I build a lazy delayed-array pipeline and collect the result?
a: Wrap a matrix with delarr::delarr(), queue lazy verbs like delarr::d_center(), delarr::d_map(), and delarr::d_reduce(), then materialize once with delarr::collect(). This keeps intermediate transforms lazy while letting the final reduction execute in one pipeline.
recipe:
mat <- matrix(rnorm(20), nrow = 5, ncol = 4)
out <- delarr::delarr(mat) |>
  delarr::d_center(dim = "rows", na.rm = TRUE) |>
  delarr::d_map(~ .x * 0.5) |>
  delarr::d_reduce(mean, dim = "rows") |>
  delarr::collect()

q: How do I lazily transform an HDF5 dataset and write the result back to disk?
a: Use delarr::delarr_hdf5() to stream the source dataset, queue a transform such as delarr::d_zscore(), then pass delarr::hdf5_writer() to delarr::collect() so the result is written chunk-by-chunk without materializing the full matrix in memory.
recipe:
src <- delarr::delarr_hdf5("input.h5", "X")
out <- src |>
  delarr::d_zscore(dim = "cols")
writer <- delarr::hdf5_writer(
  path = "output.h5",
  dataset = "X_z",
  ncol = dim(src)[2],
  chunk = c(128L, 4096L)
)
delarr::collect(out, into = writer)

q: How do I wrap a custom slice function as a delarr backend?
a: Use delarr::delarr_backend() with matrix dimensions and a pull(rows, cols) function that returns slices from your source. The result behaves like any other delarr object, so you can add lazy transforms and finish with delarr::collect().
